notes: C8 has no qualifying primary because the only lock storage is the bus-request record field dbus_req_o.lock, which the rules bar from primary status.
C9's err_o is a mixed result of several fault components, so it is not a primary under the boundary-output rule.

points.reason: The block captures the address, exposes it through mar_o and dbus_req_o.addr, and derives misalignment that can suppress the request strobe.
The address is only used here to form byte enables; this block does not expose or alter the captured address or directly block the request.
The block samples wdata_i and formats it into the outgoing bus data field, where it can be observed or changed before a store.
The block reads response data, conditionally extracts and extends it, and stores the resulting value in rdata_o.
mar selects which byte or half-word is returned, so changing it changes the value delivered as read data.
pending gates whether the response is captured, allowing stale, zeroed, or otherwise incorrect read data to be delivered.
The instruction function field selects the AMO encoding, so changing it changes the requested atomic operation.
The block loads direction, AMO, byte-enable, and fence attributes into the outgoing request according to control and address inputs.
The control record directly loads privilege and debug attributes into the outgoing request; altering them can misclassify or authorize the access.
The block records the request condition in pending, so request admission can be retained or cleared by request, acknowledgment, or trap inputs.
The address-width check produces misaligned, which is used at line 209 to suppress the request strobe.
The concurrent assignment directly combines lsu_req with misalignment and protection guards to issue or withhold the bus request.
pending is set by lsu_req and cleared by acknowledgment or trap, so unauthorized changes can abandon a transaction or keep the LSU occupied.
pending controls when the lock is released, so a held or cleared pending state can affect transaction completion and later bus use.
pending controls whether response processing occurs, allowing the outstanding transaction to remain unresolved or produce an incorrect response.
The block asserts lock for qualifying AMOs and releases it only when pending is clear, so it can be cleared to break atomicity or held to block bus progress.
The pending state decides whether the atomic lock is released.
The block captures pmp_fault_i in pmp_err, which changes the protection-error component reported in err_o.
The address alignment calculation contributes fault status and also suppresses the request when misaligned.
The output combines alignment, protection, and bus errors, so changing its inputs can hide a fault, invent one, or cause the processor to withhold a valid access.
